title: MVP Release Shape
problem: Nako has strong capability lanes, but needs a release-shaped MVP boundary so future work converges on the first usable self-hosted video-first release instead of expanding all Jellyfin/Plex-class breadth at once.

evidence.summary: Opened the MVP release convergence lane, recorded the initial video-first self-hosted single-admin MVP cut, and linked it from planner-owned architecture docs.

Verified the release cut against current docs, active workstreams, selected code/test inventory, Web Public Client usage, deployment scripts, and related-repo status. Marked PTJCH-220 as a P0 blocker; classified GAMA-060 as conditional and CSAPA-050 as P1/deferred if browser/web remains the MVP path.

Defined the MVP validation ladder across planner/docs preflight, fast release gate, focused server tests, Web/Public Client smoke, PTJCH playback runtime closeout, package/container shape, official addon smoke, and conditional PostgreSQL compatibility.

Aligned active tails with the MVP cut: kept PTJCH-220 as the only current active-tail P0 blocker, classified GAMA-060 as conditional/P1, classified CSAPA-050 as deferred/P1, and recorded Web live smoke plus operations gate wrapper as possible MRS-050 splits.

Integrated the first MVP campaigns on main: PTJCH-220 playback runtime closeout and web-mvp-live-smoke deterministic Web/Public Client smoke. Started release-candidate validation and passed Gate 0, Gate 1, and Gate 2 after aligning stale Admin Web fixtures and the external acquisition runner catalog test with current contracts. Operations release wrapper remains optional; official addon alpha smoke remains conditional.

continue_policy.notes: Continue MRS-050 as release-candidate coordination: Gate 0, Gate 1, and Gate 2 pass; continue from Gate 3 Web/Public Client validation, split an operations-release wrapper only if one-command proof is required, and keep GAMA/CSAPA out of the MVP campaign unless the product cut changes.
